mainTopic: How a father and a husband can cancel (הפרה) a girl's vows before her marriage, and whether a husband can cancel a vow he never heard (הפרה בלא שמיעה)
overview: The משנה describes a custom of תלמידי חכמים: before a daughter marries, her father cancels all the vows she made in his house. The husband does the same before she enters his רשות, because afterward he can no longer cancel her earlier vows. In the גמרא, רמי בר חמא asks whether a husband can cancel a vow he never heard. רבא tries to prove from the משנה that he can, but the גמרא answers that the father's words only take effect when he actually hears each vow. He speaks up early because a scholar makes a point of pursuing such matters. The גמרא gives the same answer to proofs from the husband in the משנה and from רבי אליעזר's case of a husband leaving on a trip, adding that he speaks in advance in case he is too busy when he hears. Finally, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about a husband who appoints an אפוטרופוס to cancel his wife's vows. Since everyone agrees that an agent is like the person who sent him, and the agent never heard the vows, it seems hearing is not required. Whether this proof holds continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The father cancels his daughter's vows before she marries
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says it is the practice of תלמידי חכמים that a father, before his daughter leaves him to marry, tells her that all the vows she made in his house are cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practice of תלמידי חכמים: before his daughter leaves him, the father says to her, 'All vows you made in my house are cancelled.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes a good custom. A wise father cancels all of his daughter's vows right before she leaves his home to get married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father has the power of הפרה over his young daughter's vows. Scholars use that power at the last moment, so she does not carry old vows into her marriage. Notice that he speaks about all vows in general, without naming any specific vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Torah scholars
Vows
Cancelled (annulled through הפרה)

phrases.english: MISHNA: The practice of Torah scholars:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה בִּתּוֹ יוֹצְאָה מֵאֶצְלוֹ,
phrases.english: before his daughter would leave him,
he says to her:
All vows that you vowed in my house
are hereby cancelled.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholarly father cancels all of his daughter's vows in a general statement before she leaves for marriage.

steps.title: The husband does the same before she enters his domain
steps.stepSummary: The husband also cancels her earlier vows before she enters his רשות, because once she does, he can no longer cancel them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise the husband, before she enters his domain, says to her, 'All vows you made before you entered my domain are cancelled,' because once she enters his domain he cannot cancel them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that the husband follows the same custom while she is still only betrothed. It also gives the reason: after she fully enters his רשות, it is too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vows she made before entering his רשות can only be cancelled while she is still betrothed, before the full marriage. Once she enters his domain, he loses the power to cancel those earlier vows. So the husband has to act in time.

keyTerms.meaning: Husband
His domain, meaning the stage when she fully marries and comes under his authority
To cancel a vow

steps.whatToRemember: Both father and husband cancel her vows in advance, with a general statement, before the marriage is complete.

phrases.english: And likewise the husband,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּכָּנֵס לִרְשׁוּתוֹ, אוֹמֵר לָהּ:
phrases.english: before she enters his domain, says to her:
All vows that you vowed
before you entered my domain
are hereby cancelled.
For once she enters his domain,
he cannot cancel them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הַבַּעַל, עַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּכָּנֵס לִרְשׁוּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the father's custom to the husband and gives the reason for the timing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband cancels her earlier vows before she enters his רשות, since afterward he cannot.

steps.title: Can a husband cancel a vow he never heard?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks whether the words 'and her husband hears' in the פסוק are a requirement, or just a description of the usual case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: Can a husband cancel a vow without hearing it? Is 'and her husband hears' meant exactly, or not exactly?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question. Does a husband have to actually hear about a vow in order to cancel it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of the husband hearing the vow. If that word is דווקא (exact), hearing is a requirement and a blind general cancellation does nothing. If it is לאו דווקא, the Torah is only describing what normally happens, and he can cancel without hearing.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked, posed a question
Hearing (about the vow)
Exactly, meant as a strict requirement
Not exactly, just describing the usual case

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rami bar Chama asked:
A husband: may he cancel without hearing?
Is 'and her husband hears' meant exactly,
or is it not meant exactly?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question that the משנה's general cancellation will be used to address.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether hearing the vow is a requirement for the husband's הפרה.

steps.title: רבא brings a proof from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא points to the משנה: the father cancels all vows from his house, yet he never heard them, so hearing must not be required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. The practice of תלמידי חכמים: before his daughter leaves him, he says to her, 'All vows you made in my house are cancelled.' But he did not hear them!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question with a proof from our משנה. A father cancels vows he never heard, so a vow can be cancelled without hearing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's general statement covers vows he knows nothing about. If the cancellation works, then hearing is not a requirement. The גמרא repeats the משנה's words here on purpose, to use them as evidence.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a proof
But he did not hear!

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
The practice of Torah scholars:
before his daughter left him,
he says to her:
All vows that you vowed in my house
are hereby cancelled,
but he did not hear them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר חמא's question using the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's general cancellation by the father of vows he never heard.

steps.title: The cancellation only works once he hears
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the father's statement only takes effect at the moment he actually hears each vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he hears, that is when he cancels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof. The father's words may be set up in advance, but each vow only becomes cancelled when he actually hears it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reads the משנה differently. The statement is not a blind cancellation right now. It is a cancellation that kicks in later, upon hearing, so hearing could still be required and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: When he will hear
Cancels

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the father's statement is useless. It says the statement takes effect only later, when he hears the vow.

phrases.english: When he hears, that is when he cancels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof by reading the משנה another way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. It does not decide רמי בר חמא's question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the cancellation takes effect immediately, but it may only take effect upon hearing.

steps.title: Then why say it before he hears?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading: if the vow is only cancelled when he hears it, why make a statement in advance at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, when he has not heard, why does he need to say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection it just gave. If the father can only cancel once he hears, there seems to be no point in speaking up early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the new reading, he could simply wait and cancel each vow when he hears it. So the advance statement seems to do nothing. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why does he need to say it?

phrases.english: If so, when he has not heard,
why does he need to say it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, כִּי לָא שְׁמַע, לְמָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the father's cancellation only takes effect upon hearing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it only works later, upon hearing, the advance statement seems pointless.

steps.title: A scholar makes a point of pursuing these matters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה teaches that a צורבא מרבנן goes out of his way to deal with such matters, even before they come up.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us: it is the way of a צורבא מרבנן to pursue these matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Speaking up in advance shows the scholar's eagerness to take care of her vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The advance statement is not what cancels the vows. It shows a scholar going after the matter, which can prompt her to tell him her vows so he can cancel them when he hears. So the רישא of the משנה does not prove that a husband can cancel without hearing, and the גמרא looks for another proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
His way, his practice
A young Torah scholar
To pursue, to go after

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof from the משנה fails: the father's statement may only take effect when he hears, and he says it early because a scholar goes out of his way to handle such matters.

phrases.english: This teaches us:
It is the way of a young Torah scholar to pursue it.
phrases.notes: He goes after it so she will tell him her vows, and then he can cancel them once he hears.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 and keeps the rejection of step 5 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new purpose for the statement (showing the scholar's eagerness) instead of a legal effect.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The advance statement seemed pointless if cancellation only happens upon hearing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The statement shows a scholar's practice of pursuing such matters, so the משנה is no proof that hearing is not required.

steps.title: A proof from the end of the משנה about a husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from the סיפא of the משנה that a husband can cancel vows he never heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the end of the משנה: and likewise the husband, before she enters his domain, says to her (all your vows are cancelled).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof from the end of the same משנה. A husband cancels his wife's vows before she even comes into his home, so he clearly did not hear them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4's proof was from the father, and step 5 pushed it away. Now the גמרא tries the same idea with the בעל. He cancels her vows in advance without hearing them, which would mean hearing is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is about to bring a source as a proof
The later part of a משנה or ברייתא
Husband
Domain or authority; here, coming into the husband's home after the wedding

phrases.english: Come and hear from the latter clause:
phrases.notes: This is the later part of the same משנה that רבא quoted about the father in step 4.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הַבַּעַל, עַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּכָּנֵס לִרְשׁוּתוֹ,
phrases.english: And similarly the husband, before she enters his domain,
says to her (your vows are cancelled).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the father proof was answered, the גמרא tries a parallel proof from the husband in the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband can cancel vows without hearing them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: a husband cancels vows before she enters his domain.

steps.title: The husband also means 'when I hear it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the husband's advance statement only takes effect when he hears each vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is where he said to her: 'when I hear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the proof away with the same answer it gave about the father. The husband's words only work once he actually hears the vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's early statement is like a cancellation waiting to happen. It takes effect at the moment of hearing, so hearing is still part of the process and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too: the same answer as before applies
When I hear: the cancellation takes effect at the moment of hearing

phrases.english: Here too, it is where he said to her:
"When I hear."
phrases.notes: He means: each vow becomes cancelled at the moment I find out about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 8 using the same explanation as step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the husband in the סיפא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the cancellation works with no hearing, but it may only take effect when he hears.

steps.title: A proof from a husband who cancels all vows until he returns from a trip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה where רבי אליעזר says a husband's advance cancellation works, even though he never heard the vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one who says to his wife, 'All vows you make until I come back from such-and-such a place are confirmed' has said nothing. If he says 'they are cancelled,' רבי אליעזר says they are cancelled. But he did not hear them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another משנה. A husband cancels ahead of time all vows his wife will make while he is away, and רבי אליעזר says it works, even though he never heard them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the vows do not even exist yet, and the husband will be far away. Since רבי אליעזר still says they are cancelled, it seems hearing cannot be a requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: Confirmed: the vows stay in force
Cancelled
He has said nothing: his words have no effect
The תנא who says the advance cancellation works

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who says to his wife,
"All vows that you will vow
until I come back from such-and-such a place

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הֵן קַיָּימִין״ — לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: are hereby confirmed" has said nothing.
If he said "they are hereby cancelled,"
Rabbi Eliezer says: it is cancelled.
But he did not hear!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof for the same question after the previous one was rejected.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband can cancel vows without hearing them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה where רבי אליעזר rules that an advance cancellation of future vows works.

steps.title: Again: he meant 'when I hear it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this husband also meant his cancellation to take effect when he hears each vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is where he said: 'when I hear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes this proof away the same way it handled the others. The husband meant the vows would be cancelled once he hears them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's ruling can be read as an advance statement that only kicks in when the husband learns of each vow. So this משנה does not prove that hearing is unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancelling a vow (the topic of the whole discussion)
Hearing: the husband finding out about the vow
That he said: the גמרא explains what the speaker meant

phrases.english: Here too, it is where he said: "When I hear."

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי אליעזר's ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case can be explained as a cancellation that takes effect upon hearing.

steps.title: Then why cancel in advance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the cancellation only works when he hears, why not just cancel when he hears?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need it from now? When he hears, let him cancel it for her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the vow only becomes cancelled at the moment he hears it, the advance statement seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of challenge as step 6, now aimed at the husband going on a trip. If hearing is needed anyway, he could simply cancel the vow at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? Asks what purpose something serves
From now: in advance
Let him cancel

phrases.english: And why do I need it from now?
When he hears, let him cancel it for her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the husband said 'when I hear.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the cancellation only works upon hearing, saying it in advance adds nothing.

steps.title: He might be too busy when he hears
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the husband worries he will be busy at the moment he hears and forget to cancel.
steps.simpleTranslation: He reasons: perhaps I will be busy at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the advance statement is useful. The husband fears that when he hears the vow he will be distracted and forget to cancel it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cancelling has to happen on the day he hears the vow, and a busy person could let that time slip by. By speaking in advance, the cancellation happens on its own at the moment of hearing. So the 'when I hear' reading still makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds / he reasons
Perhaps
I will be busy or distracted
That moment

phrases.english: He reasons: perhaps I will be busy
at that moment.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a practical reason for the advance statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying it in advance seems useless if hearing is needed anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: It protects against forgetting to cancel when he is busy at the time he hears.
steps.whatToRemember: Each proof so far has been pushed away the same way: the advance cancellation only takes effect when the husband (or father) actually hears the vow.

steps.title: Setting up a proof from a husband who appoints an אפוטרופוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a husband who tells his אפוטרופוס to cancel his wife's vows. רבי יאשיה says it does not work, because only the husband may cancel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one who says to his אפוטרופוס, 'All vows my wife makes from now until I come back from such-and-such a place, cancel them,' and he cancelled them. You might think they are cancelled. The פסוק says: 'Her husband may confirm it and her husband may cancel it.' These are the words of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof from a ברייתא. A husband asks his אפוטרופוס to cancel his wife's future vows, and רבי יאשיה rules that only the husband himself can cancel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה rejects the אפוטרופוס only because the פסוק says 'her husband,' meaning the husband personally. He does not object that the husband never heard the vows. The גמרא will draw its point from this in what follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A manager appointed to run someone's affairs
You might think: introduces a possibility the פסוק rules out
The פסוק teaches
Her husband may confirm it and her husband may cancel it
The תנא who teaches that only the husband may cancel

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who says to a steward,
"All vows that my wife vows

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן וְעַד שֶׁאָבֹא מִמָּקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי הָפֵר״,
phrases.english: from now until I come back from such-and-such a place, cancel,"
and he cancelled for her,
you might think they would be cancelled;
therefore the verse says:
"Her husband may confirm it and her husband may cancel it."
These are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the previous proof was answered, the גמרא brings a new source to test the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether hearing is required for a husband's cancellation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a husband who tells his אפוטרופוס to cancel his wife's future vows, with רבי יאשיה's ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יאשיה rejects the אפוטרופוס because only the husband himself may cancel. His reason has nothing to do with whether anyone heard the vows.

steps.title: רבי יונתן says the agent can cancel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן disagrees with רבי יאשיה and says the אפוטרופוס can cancel the vows, because a person's agent counts like the person himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said to him: We find everywhere in the whole Torah that a person's agent is like himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the other side of the argument. רבי יונתן says the steward's cancellation does work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה said only the husband himself may cancel. רבי יונתן answers with a general Torah rule, שלוחו של אדם כמותו: an agent acts with the full power of the person who sent him. So the steward can cancel just as the husband could.

keyTerms.meaning: A person's agent is like himself (what the agent does counts as if the sender did it)
We have found
In the entire Torah, everywhere

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the line ends with a question mark, רבי יונתן is not unsure. He means: "Don't we find everywhere in the Torah that an agent counts like the person?"

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said to him:
We have found in the entire Torah
that a person's agent is like himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 14 by giving רבי יונתן's opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אפוטרופוס appointed by the husband can cancel the wife's vows, since a person's agent is like himself.

steps.title: Everyone agrees on agency, yet the agent never heard the vows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that even רבי יאשיה accepts agency in general and blocks it only because of a verse. So according to everyone, an agent who never heard the vows would be able to cancel them, which shows hearing is not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רבי יאשיה only said it does not work because it is a special rule of the verse, "Her husband may uphold it and her husband may cancel it." But according to everyone, a person's agent is like himself. And yet the agent never heard the vows!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the point it wanted from this ברייתא. It shows that the agent's cancellation would work even though he never heard the vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה's only problem is the verse that says "her husband", which requires the husband himself. Without that verse, both sides agree an agent could cancel. The גמרא argues that such an agent never heard the wife vow, so it seems hearing should not be required for הפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A special rule set by the verse, not based on general logic
"Her husband may uphold it and her husband may cancel it" (במדבר 30:14)
According to everyone
But he did not hear it!

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree that agency works in general. רבי יאשיה blocks it only because of the verse. The גמרא uses this to argue that hearing is not required, because the agent never hears the vows. This is a proof being offered, not yet a final ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a fresh attempt to answer רמי בר חמא's question from step 3. Unlike the earlier proofs, it is built on the rule of agency that both תנאים accept, not on how someone's words are read. Whether this proof holds is taken up on the next amud.

phrases.english: And even Rabbi Yoshiya only said it
because it is a special rule of the verse:
"Her husband may uphold it and her husband may cancel it,"
but according to everyone
a person's agent is like himself.
And yet he did not hear it!
phrases.notes: "He" is the agent. He never heard the wife make the vows, yet being an agent would still let him cancel them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה לָא קָאָמַר אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דִּגְזֵירַת הַכָּתוּב הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical lesson from the ברייתא quoted in steps 14 and 15.
steps.raayaObject: That הפרה can work even if the one cancelling never heard the vow.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the אפוטרופוס: both רבי יונתן and רבי יאשיה accept agency in general, and the agent never heard the vows.
